command: ETLANTIC_CP_TEST_URL=<local PostgreSQL+psycopg URL> uv run pytest -q tests/prefect/test_managed_prefect_0_58.py::test_process_worker_executes_targeted_csv_and_postgresql_transfers
result: Workspace-source live Process-worker test passed: 1 passed in 20.24s.
assertions: A real Process worker was hard-killed after writing a partial source-artifact staging file but before the atomic rename; the destination artifact and durable result publication did not exist, and PostgreSQL showed no sink write or effect-ledger record.
The managed artifact store used the run-scoped workspace lock as its write serialization boundary, so no crash-persistent per-file lock blocked recovery.

Recovery marked the first attempt lost, executed a second attempt, removed the abandoned staging file for that exact artifact destination, wrote a complete JSON artifact, and published a successful report.

The recovered PostgreSQL sink contained the expected row and exactly one effect-ledger record; the durable execution effect was committed and the artifact JSON matched the accepted CSV row. The same trace rotates the sink credential after dispatch and before claim; the worker succeeds with the rotated role, while neither old nor new password appears in the accepted execution snapshot.

runtime.prefect_server: Separately supervised API process backed by PostgreSQL
runtime.worker_backend_plugin: Repository integration-test fixture imported through its temporary test entry-point shim; not an installed-wheel run

source_sha256_method: SHA-256 over sorted repository-relative source paths and file bytes, with NUL separators.
limitations: This trace covers a process hard kill while writing a managed durable artifact before an external effect. It does not claim power-loss durability across filesystem or device failure, crash points in report storage, or recovery of non-transactional connector partial effects.
This is local workspace-source evidence for CPython 3.11.15, Prefect 3.7.8, PostgreSQL 16.13, and the Process pool; remote CI and the complete supported-version and hosting matrix remain open.
